tools.name: data_status
tools.description: Inspect before health reviews or investigating missing data. Returns the last received upload batch, collection date ranges/counts and per-metric coverage. Not a sync command. history_import is the iPhone's own report of its history import (complete, still arriving, or unknown for older app builds);

tools.name: list_metrics
tools.description: Lists the available health metrics, the unit of each one, and how far back the data goes. Call this before query_daily if you do not know the exact metric names.

tools.name: query_daily
tools.description: Daily records or week/month aggregates. aggregation identifies sum or unweighted average of stored daily values; daily_min/max are extrema of daily values, not raw samples. days_present counts stored dates; days_expected counts calendar dates in period_start/end clipped to the request, not expected

tools.name: workout_detail
tools.description: Detail for a workout UUID from sessions. Includes source/device, indoor flag, pool length, elevation gain, laps, classified segments, paired pause intervals, a swimming summary and reduced series when accessible in HealthKit. Summaries, events and zones are permanent; only raw series expire after 30

tools.name: home
tools.description: Read the cards on the user's telo iPhone home screen, the dated marks they asked you to keep (e.g. 'Sick', 'Intervals start'), and recent changes. Marks are context the user gave about their life; use them when interpreting their data. Call before editing the home.

tools.name: pin_card
tools.description: Put a live chart on the user's telo iPhone home. Only when the user asks to pin, save, show or keep something on telo. The card keeps updating with each sync. Styles: trend (line), stat (number and change), bars. Optional: compare_with draws a second metric on the same window; baseline=personal draw

tools.name: pin_countdown
tools.description: Add a countdown to a date the user named (a race, a trip, a test) to their telo home. telo counts days; it never judges them.

tools.name: edit_card
tools.description: Change one card: title, window, style, comparison, usual range, color, size, change_from, or a goal the user stated. null removes an option. Call home first for ids.

tools.name: arrange_home
tools.description: Reorder cards, remove cards or remove marks, when the user asks to set up or tidy their home (e.g. 'set my home up for race week'). The reason is shown to the user in the change history, and every change can be undone on the phone.

tools.name: mark_date
tools.description: Keep a short note the user told you about a date or span (illness, travel, new training, new shoes). It appears on every telo chart covering that date and is returned by home to any assistant later. Only for facts the user stated, never your inference.

tools.name: report_gap
tools.description: Call when the user asked for something telo cannot do with the tools here: a chart or layout on the telo home, a metric telo does not have, data that is missing, a question no tool answers. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_workout_plan, workout_plans, data_status · Private data: data_status, query_daily · Public sink: create_workout_plan, data_status, workout_detail · Destructive: cancel_workout_plan, sessions, arrange_home.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_workout_plan, workout_plans, data_status · Private data: data_status, query_daily · Public sink: create_workout_plan, data_status, workout_detail · Destructive: cancel_workout_plan, sessions, arrange_home

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
